examples.en: I was a student then.
I still remember what happened then.
I was too young then to know.
I'll wait here until then.

examples.ko: 그때의 나와 지금의 나는 많이 달라요.
examples.en: The me of that time and the me of now are very different.

examples.ko: 우리 그때 같이 간 식당 기억나요?
examples.en: Do you remember the restaurant we went to together back then?

explain: '지금'은 말하는 순간, '그때'는 이미 이야기에 나온 시점이에요. 한 단어라서 '그 때'가 아니라 붙여 써요. '그때그때 달라요'처럼 반복해서 '그 상황마다'라는 뜻으로도 써요.

phrases.en: Back then, I was young.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 시점을 다른 때와 비교할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to contrast that time with another.

phrases.en: We became friends from then on.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 시점에서 시작할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something starting from that point.

phrases.en: The menu changes depending on the day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상황마다 다르다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it differs by each situation.

explain_en: Neutral — a time mentioned or past or future point (그때 만나요) '지금' is the moment of speaking, while '그때' points to a time already mentioned. It is one word, written '그때', not '그 때'. Repeated as '그때그때' it means 'depending on the occasion', as in '그때그때 달라요'.

examples.en: In the evening Mom cooks and I do the dishes.
I'm tired today, so I don't feel like cooking.
I got home from work and cooked right away.
On weekends Dad cooks for us.
While cooking the rice, I also boiled soup.

examples.ko: 밥할 시간이 없을 때는 햇반을 먹어요.
examples.en: When I have no time to cook, I eat instant rice.

explain: 쌀로 밥을 짓는 것이 기본이지만, 집에서 식사를 준비한다는 넓은 뜻으로도 자주 말해요. '밥을 짓다'는 조금 글 같은 느낌이고, 말할 때는 '밥하다'나 '밥을 하다'가 편해요. '요리하다'는 반찬이나 여러 음식을 만드는 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.en: I cook rice and eat at home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직접 밥을 만들어서 먹는다는 뜻으로, 밖에서 사 먹는 것과 비교할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to cook and eat yourself; often contrasted with buying food outside.
phrases.en_equiv: to cook and eat at home

phrases.en: My mom cooks for me every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람을 위해 밥을 만들어 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone cooks a meal for another person.

phrases.en: Who cooked today?
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로 물을 때 써요. 친한 사이에서는 '밥했어?'라고 반말로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past-tense question; among close friends you can say '밥했어?' in casual speech.

explain_en: Its core meaning is cooking rice, but people often use it more broadly for preparing meals at home. '밥을 짓다' sounds a bit more written, so in speech '밥하다' or '밥을 하다' is natural. '요리하다' feels more like making side dishes or various foods.

examples.en: I gave my friend pretty flowers for her birthday.

examples.ko: 이번 어버이날에 어머니께 스카프를 선물할 거예요.
examples.en: I'm going to give my mother a scarf for Parents' Day.

examples.ko: 한국 사람들은 집들이에 보통 뭘 선물해요?
examples.en: What do Koreans usually give as a gift at a housewarming?

examples.ko: 선생님께 직접 만든 카드를 선물해 드렸어요.
examples.en: I gave my teacher a handmade card as a gift.
I want to give my friend a Korean book.
What could I give the child that they would like?

explain: 받는 사람이 정해져 있어서 'A에게 B를 선물하다'로 써요. 윗사람에게는 '어머니께 선물해 드렸어요'처럼 '드리다'를 붙여요. '선물을 주다'도 자주 쓰고, 반대로 받는 쪽은 '선물을 받다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I gave my friend a present.
phrases.nuance_ko: '선물하다'와 뜻이 같고, 더 쉽게 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 선물하다 and an easier, common expression.

phrases.en: I gave my grandmother a hat as a gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람에게 선물할 때 '드리다'를 붙여 높여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 드리다 to show respect when giving to an elder.

phrases.en: I want to give flowers to my mom as a gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 싶다'를 붙여서 선물하고 싶은 마음을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -고 싶다 expresses the wish to give a gift.

explain_en: The receiver is always clear: 'A에게 B를 선물하다'. For someone older, add '드리다', as in '어머니께 선물해 드렸어요'. '선물을 주다' is also common, and the receiving side is '선물을 받다'.

examples.ko: 처음에는 양을 채우고, 질은 그다음에 올려요.
examples.en: First you fill up the amount, and raise the quality after that.
Whose turn is next?
The next morning the rain stopped.

examples.ko: 이 길로 쭉 가서 그다음 사거리에서 오른쪽으로 가세요.
examples.en: Go straight along this road and turn right at the next intersection.
From then on, I'll take care of it myself.

examples.ko: 가장 중요한 건 건강이고, 그다음으로 가족이에요.
examples.en: The most important thing is health, and after that, family.

explain: '다음'은 그냥 뒤에 오는 것이고, '그다음'은 방금 말한 것이나 앞의 순서를 기준으로 바로 뒤를 가리켜요. 말할 때는 '그담에'로 줄여서 말하기도 해요. '그다음 날, 그다음 문제'처럼 뒤에 명사를 바로 붙여도 돼요.

phrases.en: We met again the next day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에서 말한 날의 바로 뒷날을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the day right after the day just mentioned.

phrases.en: What did you do after that?
phrases.nuance_ko: '에'를 붙여서 이야기의 순서를 이어 갈 때 가장 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '에', the most common way to continue the order of events in a story.

phrases.en: Wash first, and then eat.
phrases.nuance_ko: '그다음에'를 줄인 말투라서 대화에서 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of '그다음에', used casually in conversation.

explain_en: Next step in a sequence; spoken, neutral. '다음' is simply what comes later, while '그다음' points to what comes right after the thing or step just mentioned. In speech it is often shortened to '그담에'. You can put a noun right after it, as in '그다음 날' or '그다음 문제'.

examples.en: I wrote my name in big letters on my bag with a marker.
Marker writing doesn't come off easily.
Make sure to keep the marker's cap closed.
The child scribbled on the wall with a marker.
Please lend me just one black marker.
The marker smells a bit.

explain: 글씨가 잘 지워지지 않아서 이름을 쓰거나 큰 글씨를 쓸 때 써요. 같은 종류를 '네임펜'이라고도 해요. '사인펜'은 따로 있는 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: I wrote my name with a permanent marker.
phrases.nuance_ko: 매직펜과 같은 종류를 부르는 다른 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Another name for the same kind of pen as 매직펜.

phrases.en: Please write it big with a marker.
phrases.nuance_ko: 펜 이름 뒤에 '(으)로'를 붙여 도구를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add (으)로 after the pen name to show the tool.

phrases.en: Please give me one black marker.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색깔을 앞에 붙여서 필요한 펜을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the color before it to say which marker you need.

explain_en: Its writing doesn't come off easily, so it is used for writing names or large letters. The same kind of pen is also called '네임펜'. '사인펜' is a different word for a different kind of pen.

examples.en: I filled the water glass to the brim.
Please bring two water glasses.
When I do the dishes, I wash the water glasses first.

explain: '컵'은 종이컵, 머그컵처럼 종류가 많아서 물 마시는 용도를 분명히 할 때 '물컵'이라고 해요. 비슷한 말로 '물잔'도 있어요. 물은 '따르다'와 함께 써서 '물컵에 물을 따르다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I put ice in the water glass.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물컵과 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A word similar to 물컵.

phrases.en: I washed the water glass while doing the dishes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 설거지할 때 '씻다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 씻다 (to wash) when doing dishes.

phrases.en: Please give me one more water glass.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당이나 집에서 컵을 더 달라고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to ask for one more glass at a restaurant or home.

explain_en: '컵' covers many kinds, such as paper cups and mugs, so '물컵' makes clear it is for drinking water. '물잔' is a similar word. It goes with '따르다', as in '물컵에 물을 따르다'.

examples.en: Please put the fruit in a plastic bag.
The plastic bag tore and the things spilled out.

examples.ko: 일회용 비닐봉지는 돈을 내고 사야 해요.
examples.en: You have to pay for single-use plastic bags.
Could you give me one more plastic bag?
I took a shopping bag instead of a plastic bag.

explain: 줄여서 그냥 '봉지'나 '비닐'이라고도 말해요. 종이로 만든 '종이봉투'와 짝으로 생각하면 편해요. 마트에서 '봉지 필요하세요?'라고 자주 물어봐요.

phrases.en: Shall I put it in a bag for you?
phrases.nuance_ko: '비닐봉지'를 줄여 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened way to say 비닐봉지.

phrases.en: I got a plastic bag at the mart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게에서 물건을 담을 봉지를 받을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when getting a bag for goods at a store.

phrases.en: Please use a paper bag instead of a plastic bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종이로 만든 봉투로, 비닐봉지와 짝으로 생각하면 편해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A bag made of paper; easy to remember as the pair of 비닐봉지.

explain_en: People often shorten it to just '봉지' or '비닐'. It helps to think of it as the counterpart of '종이봉투' (paper bag). At supermarkets you often hear '봉지 필요하세요?'.

examples.en: The shop's glass door says 'Please pull'.
A bird hit the glass door and I was startled.

examples.ko: 유리문 너머로 아이들이 노는 모습이 보여요.
examples.en: I can see the children playing beyond the glass door.
Close the glass door carefully so it doesn't break.
The whole front of this shop is glass doors.

explain: '유리창'은 열어서 바깥을 보는 창이고 '유리문'은 열고 드나드는 문이에요. 가게 입구나 베란다 문을 말할 때 자주 써요. '유리문을 밀다/당기다/열다'처럼 같이 써요.

phrases.en: I opened the glass door and went into the shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문으로 드나들 때 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic phrase for going through a door.

phrases.en: It's cold, so please close the glass door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부탁할 때 '-아 주세요'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '-a juseyo' when making a request.

phrases.en: I'll wait in front of the glass door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 만날 장소를 정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to set a meeting place.
phrases.en_equiv: in front of the glass door

explain_en: '유리창' is a window you look out of, while '유리문' is a door you go in and out through. It's often used for shop entrances or balcony doors. It goes with verbs like '밀다' (push), '당기다' (pull), and '열다' (open).

examples.ko: 이력서에 붙일 증명사진을 찍으러 사진관에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to a photo studio to get an ID photo for my résumé.

examples.ko: 증명사진이 마음에 안 들어서 다시 찍었어요.
examples.en: I didn't like my ID photo, so I had it taken again.
ID photos for passports have a set size.
There are two ID photos in my wallet.
Do you need just one more ID photo?

examples.ko: 사진관에서 증명사진을 찍는 데 만 원 들었어요.
examples.en: It cost ten thousand won to get an ID photo at the studio.

explain: 여권, 이력서, 신분증 같은 서류에 쓰는 얼굴 사진이에요. '증명사진을 찍다', '증명사진을 붙이다'처럼 써요. 그냥 '사진'이라고 하면 일상 사진도 되니까 서류용일 때 '증명사진'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I had an ID photo taken for my passport.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류에 쓸 사진을 새로 만들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when getting a new photo for documents.

phrases.en: Please attach an ID photo to the form.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류를 낼 때 사진을 붙이라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when telling someone to attach a photo to a form.

phrases.en: What size should the ID photo be?
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류마다 사진 크기가 달라서 자주 묻는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common question since photo sizes differ by document.

explain_en: It's a face photo for documents such as passports, résumés, and ID cards. Say '증명사진을 찍다' (take) and '증명사진을 붙이다' (attach). Plain '사진' can be any photo, so use '증명사진' when you mean one for documents.
